title: Reconfigurable Single-Ring Photonic Molecule On Lithium Niobate
authors: Tianyi Zhang, Andr\'e Garcia Primo, Jiawen Liu, Aleksei Gaier, Ileana-Cristina Benea-Chelmus
abstract: ArXiv:2606.06637v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Resonant photonic structures enable optical enhancement and spectral filtering and are essential for lasers, quantum emitters, transducers, or modulators. Photonic molecules, formed by mode hybridisation in two coupled resonators, break the equidistant frequency spacing of zero-dispersion resonators and provide control over their spectrum. Reconfigurability over these devices is a key asset, allowing to align photonic resonances to target frequencies on-demand. While electro-optic materials such as thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN) have enabled frequency tuning beyond traditional thermo-optic effects, they require continuous bias, posing challenges to scalability. Here we demonstrate an optically programmable, erasable, and rewritable photonic molecule realized within a single TFLN racetrack resonator. A long-lasting photorefractive grating induced through interference of co-propagating dark and bright transverse modes promotes their hybridisation, forming a single-ring photonic molecule. We observe GHz-scale hybrid-mode splitting over a 700 GHz-wide optical bandwidth and hour-long lifetimes, and show that their coupling strength can be programmed by the optical pump used to write the grating. By selectively pumping orthogonal hybridised modes, we further demonstrate multiple reversible all-optical write-erase-rewrite cycles of these gratings. Finally, we use this technique to realize single-sideband mmWave transduction around 107 GHz with a 5 GHz tuning bandwidth. These results establish photorefraction as a reliable mechanism for reconfigurable resonances in TFLN, and suggest a route towards tunable microwave-optical functionalities within a reduced footprint.

motivation: Reconfigurable photonic molecules are needed for tunable optical filtering and quantum transduction, but existing electro-optic tuning requires continuous bias, limiting scalability.
method: A photorefractive grating is induced by interfering co-propagating dark and bright transverse modes in a single TFLN racetrack resonator, creating hybridized modes that form a photonic molecule.
result: GHz-scale hybrid-mode splitting over 700 GHz bandwidth with hour-long lifetimes is achieved, and the coupling strength is programmable via optical pump power. Multiple write-erase-rewrite cycles are demonstrated, and single-sideband mmWave transduction around 107 GHz with 5 GHz tuning bandwidth is realized.
conclusion: Photorefraction provides a reliable mechanism for reconfigurable resonances in TFLN, offering a path to tunable microwave-optical functionalities in a compact footprint.

title: Contacting Josephson Junctions Via Airbridges In Superconducting Circuits
authors: Prakiran Baidya, Mom\v{c}ilo Milosavljevi\'c, Murali Krishna Kurmapu, Thomas F\"osel, Harshanth Ram Murugesan, Victor Kemme, Mojahed Jaber, Markus Sondermann, Christopher Eichler
abstract: ArXiv:2606.06951v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Superconducting circuit devices require electrical interconnects between different circuit elements on the chip, for which conventional device architectures use a combination of two structural elements: to connect non-adjacent elements in the base layer, and to connect the electrodes forming the Josephson junctions to the base layer. Bandages introduce unwanted parasitic material interfaces and increase the manufacturing complexity. Here, we overcome the limitations imposed by by establishing electrical interconnects with airbridges of varying size fabricated in a single step. The airbridges show a high yield and mechanical stability over a wide range of sizes from [MATH] to [MATH] in width and from [MATH] to [MATH] in length, and show low loss when integrated in coplanar waveguide resonators and transmon qubits. Measured relaxation times up to more than [MATH] in standard transmon geometries show that the process achieves high coherence while substantially easing and accelerating device fabrication.

method: Airbridges of varying sizes are fabricated in a single step and integrated into coplanar waveguide resonators and transmon qubits. Their performance is characterized via yield, mechanical stability, and qubit relaxation times.
result: Airbridges show high yield and mechanical stability across a wide size range. Transmon qubits with these airbridges achieve relaxation times over 100 µs, indicating low loss.
conclusion: The airbridge technique simplifies fabrication of superconducting circuits without compromising coherence, making it a practical improvement for quantum hardware.

title: Nonreciprocal Optomechanical Entanglement In An Asymmetric Fabry-Perot Cavity
authors: Jia-Kang Wu, Ning Hu, Jie-Qiao Liao, Xun-Wei Xu
abstract: ArXiv:2606.06988v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nonreciprocal transmission (classical nonreciprocity) in optomechanical systems based on asymmetric Fabry-Perot (F-P) cavities has been theoretically proposed and experimentally demonstrated. However, nonreciprocal quantum effects, particularly nonreciprocal quantum entanglement, remain unexplored in such systems. Here, we propose to generate nonreciprocal optomechanical entanglement in an asymmetric F-P cavity and discuss the connection between the nonreciprocal transmission and nonreciprocal quantum entanglement. We reproduce the nonreciprocal transmission spectra by solving the quantum Langevin equations, and then discuss the optimal parameters to achieve nonreciprocal optomechanical entanglement in the system. We show that a greater and more robust optomechanical entanglement can be approached in the asymmetric F-P cavities, in comparing with the symmetric cavities. Furthermore, we find that the degrees of classical and quantum nonreciprocities do not exhibit positive correlation as expected. Our work shows that the classical and quantum nonreciprocities can be realized simultaneously in the asymmetric F-P cavities, which provide a platform to explore the connection between classical and quantum nonreciprocities.
tldr: The paper proposes generating nonreciprocal optomechanical entanglement in an asymmetric Fabry-Perot cavity, linking classical and quantum nonreciprocity.
motivation: Nonreciprocal quantum entanglement has not been explored in asymmetric Fabry-Perot cavities, and understanding its connection to classical nonreciprocity could enable new quantum devices.
method: The authors solve quantum Langevin equations to model the optomechanical system and compute entanglement measures, comparing symmetric and asymmetric cavities.
result: Asymmetric cavities yield stronger and more robust optomechanical entanglement than symmetric ones, and classical and quantum nonreciprocities are not positively correlated.
conclusion: Asymmetric Fabry-Perot cavities provide a platform to simultaneously realize classical and quantum nonreciprocities, with potential applications in quantum information processing.

title: Experimental Demonstration Of Free-Space Unidimensional Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution Under High Detector Noise
authors: Rachita Nandan, Jayanth Ramakrishnan, Shashi Prabhakar, R. P. Singh
abstract: ArXiv:2606.07206v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Continuous-variable quantum key distribution (CV-QKD), which uses quadratures of the electromagnetic field, enables practical quantum communication using standard telecommunication technologies. Unidimensional CV-QKD (UD-CVQKD) simplifies the implementation by restricting modulation to a single quadrature. In this work, we experimentally demonstrate a free-space Gaussian-modulated UD-CVQKD system operating under a high detector electronic-noise regime (1.4 shot-noise units). The system employs polarized coherent states with signal and local oscillator co-propagating in the same spatial mode in orthogonal polarizations, ensuring stable interference. System security is analyzed under both untrusted (UTD) and trusted (TD) detector noise models. While no positive secret key rate is obtained under the UTD model, the TD model enables secure key generation over a finite range of modulation variances, highlighting the critical role of detector trust in high-noise conditions. A maximum secret key rate of 270 kbps is achieved at an optimal modulation variance of 11.57. Furthermore, secure operation requires high-transmittance (low-loss) channels under such noise conditions. This study demonstrates the practical feasibility of free-space UD-CVQKD in realistic high electronic-noise detection constraints and highlights detector electronic noise as a key limiting factor in practical systems.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of free-space unidimensional continuous-variable QKD under high detector noise, achieving secure key rates with trusted detector noise model.
motivation: Simplify CV-QKD implementation by modulating only one quadrature and test feasibility under realistic high electronic-noise conditions.
method: Free-space Gaussian-modulated UD-CVQKD with polarized coherent states and co-propagating local oscillator; security analysis under untrusted and trusted detector noise models.
result: No key rate under untrusted detector noise, but up to 270 kbps under trusted noise model at optimal modulation variance; requires low-loss channels.
conclusion: Demonstrates practical feasibility of free-space UD-CVQKD in high-noise regimes, highlighting detector electronic noise as a key limiting factor.

deep_read.methodology_analysis: The experimental setup uses polarized coherent states with signal and local oscillator co-propagating in the same spatial mode but orthogonal polarizations, which simplifies alignment and ensures stable interference. The system operates at a wavelength typical for telecom (likely 1550 nm) and uses homodyne detection. The modulation is Gaussian on a single quadrature, and the electronic noise is measured to be 1.4 SNU. Security analysis follows the standard CV-QKD framework with reverse reconciliation, considering both untrusted (where detector noise is attributed to Eve) and trusted (where detector noise is known to Alice and Bob) models. The secret key rate is computed as a function of modulation variance and channel transmittance, using realistic parameters. The analysis assumes collective attacks and asymptotic key rates.
deep_read.results_analysis: The key result is that under the untrusted detector noise model, the secret key rate is zero for all modulation variances, indicating that high electronic noise (1.4 SNU) cannot be tolerated if Eve controls the detector. However, under the trusted detector noise model, positive key rates are obtained for modulation variances between approximately 2 and 20, with a maximum of 270 kbps at variance 11.57. The key rate decreases with channel loss, and secure operation requires transmittance above about 0.8 (i.e., loss less than 1 dB). The results demonstrate that even with high electronic noise, secure key distribution is possible if the detector is trusted, but the range of achievable key rates is limited. The paper also shows that the optimal modulation variance increases with electronic noise.
strengths: Experimental demonstration under realistic high-noise conditions, addressing a practical challenge.
Clear comparison of trusted vs. untrusted detector noise models, highlighting the importance of detector characterization.
Achievement of a significant key rate (270 kbps) despite high electronic noise.
Well-structured analysis with explicit parameter values and operational conditions.
limitations: The analysis assumes asymptotic key rates and collective attacks; finite-size effects and composable security are not considered.
The system requires high-transmittance channels (loss < 1 dB), which may be challenging for long-distance free-space links.
Only a single quadrature is modulated, which may limit the key rate compared to full CV-QKD.
deep_read.connections_to_research: This work directly addresses quantum key distribution, a core application of quantum information theory and quantum optics. It explores the practical limitations of CV-QKD due to detector electronic noise, which is a key issue in quantum communication. The use of free-space channels and polarization multiplexing connects to quantum communication over atmospheric links. The security analysis under different detector models relates to quantum hacking and side-channel attacks, which are important for practical quantum cryptography.
deep_read.overall_assessment: This paper presents a valuable experimental contribution to the field of CV-QKD, demonstrating that UD-CVQKD can operate under high electronic noise conditions if the detector is trusted. The results are significant for practical implementations where detector noise is a limiting factor. The work is technically sound, with clear methodology and results. However, the requirement for low-loss channels and the assumption of trusted detector noise may limit its applicability. Overall, it is a well-executed study that advances the understanding of practical CV-QKD systems.

title: Integrated High-quality Multi-wavelength Quantum Light Source Compatible With Itu Channel Grid
authors: Jing Qiu
Yilin Yang
Chennan Wu
Jiaqi Zhao
Yuankai Liu
Yuanhua Li
Hao Li
Yuanlin Zheng
Xianfeng Chen
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 06 June 2026;
tldr: This paper demonstrates an integrated multi-wavelength quantum light source compatible with the ITU channel grid, enabling wavelength-division multiplexing for quantum networks.
motivation: Scalable quantum networks require multiple wavelength channels for efficient entanglement distribution, but existing sources lack integration and compatibility with standard telecom grids.
method: The authors fabricate a chip-scale source using nonlinear photonics to generate photon pairs at multiple ITU-grid wavelengths simultaneously, with characterization of brightness, purity, and indistinguishability.
result: The source achieves high brightness and low noise across multiple channels, with photon pairs showing high spectral purity and indistinguishability suitable for quantum networking protocols.
conclusion: This integrated multi-wavelength source is a practical building block for future quantum networks, enabling wavelength multiplexing and compatibility with existing telecom infrastructure.

title: Constant Runtime Error Mitigation Via Restricted Evolution
authors: Gaurav Saxena
Thi Ha Kyaw
abstract: npj Quantum Information, Published online: 05 June 2026;
tldr: Proposes a constant-time error mitigation technique for quantum circuits by restricting the evolution to a subspace that is resilient to certain errors.
motivation: Error mitigation is crucial for near-term quantum devices, but existing methods often require many circuit repetitions or post-processing. A constant-time approach could significantly reduce overhead.
method: The method restricts the quantum evolution to a carefully chosen subspace of the Hilbert space where errors are suppressed or have a known structure, allowing for efficient mitigation without iterative procedures.
result: Demonstrates that the restricted evolution approach achieves error mitigation with constant runtime overhead, independent of circuit depth, and shows improved fidelity on benchmark circuits.
conclusion: This technique offers a practical and scalable error mitigation strategy for near-term quantum computers, particularly useful for deep circuits where other methods become costly.

title: Programmable Assembly Of Ground State Fermionic Tweezer Arrays
authors: Naman Jain, Jin Zhang, Marcus Culemann, And Philipp M. Preiss
abstract:
Author(s): Naman Jain, Jin Zhang, Marcus Culemann, and Philipp M. Preiss

We demonstrate deterministic preparation of arbitrary two-component product states of fermionic [MATH] atoms in an [MATH] optical tweezer array, achieving motional ground-state fidelities above 98.5%. Leveraging the large differential magnetic moments for spin-resolution, with parallelized…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 223402] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates deterministic preparation of ground-state fermionic tweezer arrays with high fidelity, enabling quantum simulation and computing.
motivation: Neutral atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum information processing, but fermionic species pose challenges due to their internal state structure and interactions.
method: Uses optical tweezers with spin-resolved imaging and parallelized Raman sideband cooling to prepare arbitrary two-component product states of fermionic atoms in the motional ground state.
result: Achieves motional ground-state fidelities above 98.5% for arrays of up to 12 atoms, with deterministic loading and spin-state control.
conclusion: This work establishes fermionic tweezer arrays as a viable platform for quantum simulation and computing, with high-fidelity state preparation and readout.

title: Breakdown Of Disorder-Suppressed Floquet Heating Under Two-Frequency Driving
authors: Cooper M. Selco, Christian Bengs, Chaitali Shah, And Ashok Ajoy
abstract:
Author(s): Cooper M. Selco, Christian Bengs, Chaitali Shah, and Ashok Ajoy

Periodic (Floquet) driving enables Hamiltonian engineering and nonequilibrium phases, but interacting systems eventually heat by absorbing energy from the drive. Disorder can greatly delay this process, yielding long-lived prethermal plateaus. Here, we show that this protection can fail when pulse-t…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 136, 220801] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Disorder-suppressed Floquet heating breaks down under two-frequency driving, limiting prethermal plateaus.
motivation: Understanding how disorder protects against heating in driven quantum systems is crucial for realizing long-lived prethermal phases.
method: The authors study a disordered spin chain under two-frequency periodic driving using numerical simulations and analytical arguments.
result: Two-frequency driving destroys the disorder-induced prethermal plateau, leading to rapid heating even in the presence of strong disorder.
conclusion: Prethermalization in disordered Floquet systems is fragile to multi-frequency driving, which has implications for quantum simulation and thermodynamic control.

title: Equation-of-motion Approach To Double-excitation Dynamics Of The Extended Jaynes-Cummings Model
authors: Tao Luo, Yun-An Yan, And Haitao Cui
abstract:
Author(s): Tao Luo, Yun-An Yan, and Haitao Cui

Exact quantum master equations serve as a fundamental tool for investigating quantum dissipative dynamics. However, deriving such equations—even when possible—is extremely tedious for multistate and multiatom systems. In this work, we focus exclusively on population dynamics of the extended Jaynes-C…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062206] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Derives exact quantum master equations for population dynamics in the extended Jaynes-Cummings model with double-excitation, using an equation-of-motion approach.
motivation: Exact master equations for multistate and multiatom systems are extremely tedious to derive; this work aims to provide a systematic method for such systems.
method: Applies an equation-of-motion approach to obtain exact quantum master equations for the extended Jaynes-Cummings model, focusing on population dynamics with double excitations.
result: Successfully derives exact master equations and analyzes double-excitation dynamics, demonstrating the method's applicability to complex dissipative systems.
conclusion: The equation-of-motion approach is effective for deriving exact master equations in multistate cavity QED systems, enabling detailed study of quantum dissipative dynamics.

title: Embedding Scheme For The Maximum-independent-set Problem On Three-dimensional Rydberg-atom Arrays
authors: Rui Mao, Jin-Guo Liu, Shengminjie Chen, Jialin Zhang, And Xiaoming Sun
abstract:
Author(s): Rui Mao, Jin-Guo Liu, Shengminjie Chen, Jialin Zhang, and Xiaoming Sun

The Maximum Independent Set (MIS) problem on unit-disk graphs is an NP-hard problem that can be naturally encoded on Rydberg atom systems. While existing mapping schemes enable the encoding of arbitrary graphs, current two-dimensional (2D) embedding approaches have an [MATH] atom overhead, lim…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062420] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a 3D embedding scheme for the Maximum Independent Set problem on Rydberg atom arrays, reducing atom overhead compared to 2D approaches.
motivation: The Maximum Independent Set problem on unit-disk graphs can be naturally encoded in Rydberg atom systems, but existing 2D embeddings require large atom overhead, limiting scalability.
method: The authors design a 3D arrangement of Rydberg atoms to embed arbitrary graphs, leveraging the van der Waals interaction to encode the MIS constraint with fewer atoms.
result: The 3D embedding scheme achieves a polynomial reduction in atom count compared to 2D embeddings, enabling the solution of larger MIS instances.
conclusion: This work advances the practical implementation of quantum optimization on Rydberg platforms by improving resource efficiency.

title: Effects Of The Detection Loophole On Rival Entanglement Attestation Techniques
authors: Paranjoy Chaki, Kornikar Sen, And Ujjwal Sen
abstract:
Author(s): Paranjoy Chaki, Kornikar Sen, and Ujjwal Sen

Entanglement detection is of crucial significance to quantum technologies and yet remains a difficult enterprise. The positive partial transposition (PPT) and moment-based criteria are two key methods of entanglement detection. Among them, in an ideal setup, the PPT criterion can detect a greater vo…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062417] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies how the detection loophole affects the performance of PPT and moment-based entanglement detection criteria, finding that the PPT criterion's advantage diminishes under realistic conditions.
motivation: Entanglement detection is crucial for quantum technologies, but real-world detectors have inefficiencies (detection loophole) that can compromise the reliability of detection methods. The paper aims to compare the robustness of two key criteria under such practical constraints.
method: The authors analyze the PPT criterion and moment-based criteria in the presence of a detection loophole, using theoretical models and numerical simulations to evaluate their detection capabilities.
result: While the PPT criterion outperforms moment-based criteria in ideal setups, its advantage is significantly reduced when the detection loophole is considered, and in some regimes moment-based criteria become more effective.
conclusion: The detection loophole must be accounted for when choosing entanglement detection methods, and moment-based criteria may be preferable in practical scenarios with detector inefficiencies.

title: Generation Of Energy-time-entangled Triphotons In A Six-level Cold Atomic System
authors: Ling Niu, Zhiying Duan, Na Liu, Yitong Zhai, Shaoyan Liu, Junsheng Li, Donghai Zhang, And Da Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Ling Niu, Zhiying Duan, Na Liu, Yitong Zhai, Shaoyan Liu, Junsheng Li, Donghai Zhang, and Da Zhang

Multiphoton entangled states are pivotal resources for implementing optical quantum information protocols. Recently, energy-time-entangled triphotons have been observed in hot atomic ensembles. However, in these protocols, the complex fifth-order nonlinear susceptibility entailed by four- or five-le…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 063708] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: Generation of energy-time-entangled triphotons in a six-level cold atomic system via spontaneous four-wave mixing.
motivation: Multiphoton entangled states are essential for quantum information protocols, but generating energy-time-entangled triphotons with high efficiency and low noise remains challenging.
method: A six-level cold atomic system is used to realize spontaneous four-wave mixing, producing energy-time-entangled triphotons with controlled nonlinear susceptibility.
result: The scheme generates energy-time-entangled triphotons with improved efficiency and reduced noise compared to previous hot atomic ensemble approaches.
conclusion: This work provides a practical method for generating multiphoton entanglement, which can be used in quantum networks and quantum communication protocols.

title: Revealing Emergent Many-body Phenomena By Analyzing Large-scale Space-time Records Of Monitored Quantum Systems
authors: Marcel Cech, Cecilia de Fazio, María Cea, Mari Carmen Bañuls, Igor Lesanovsky, And Federico Carollo
abstract:
Author(s): Marcel Cech, Cecilia De Fazio, María Cea, Mari Carmen Bañuls, Igor Lesanovsky, and Federico Carollo

Midcircuit measurements allow the probing of quantum many-body dynamics with spatial and temporal resolution. In this work, the authors discuss how these records can reveal emergent many-body phenomena in space-time.


[Phys. Rev. A 113, L060201] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: The paper uses midcircuit measurements to reveal emergent many-body phenomena in monitored quantum systems, analyzing space-time records.
motivation: Understanding emergent phenomena in quantum many-body systems is crucial, and midcircuit measurements offer a way to probe dynamics with high resolution.
method: The authors analyze large-scale space-time records obtained from monitored quantum systems, likely using numerical simulations or theoretical frameworks.
result: They demonstrate that these records can reveal emergent many-body phenomena, such as phase transitions or dynamical patterns.
conclusion: Midcircuit measurements are a powerful tool for uncovering emergent behavior in quantum many-body systems, with implications for quantum thermodynamics and information processing.

title: Hamiltonian Simulation With Explicit Formulas For Digital-analog Quantum Computing
authors: Mikel Garcia de Andoin, Thorge Müller, And Gonzalo Camacho
abstract:
Author(s): Mikel Garcia de Andoin, Thorge Müller, and Gonzalo Camacho

Digital-analog is a quantum computational paradigm that employs the natural interaction Hamiltonian of a system as the entangling resource, combined with single qubit gates, to implement universal quantum operations. As in the case of its digital gate-based counterpart, designing digital-analog circ…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062607] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents explicit formulas for Hamiltonian simulation in the digital-analog quantum computing paradigm, leveraging natural interaction Hamiltonians.
motivation: Digital-analog quantum computing offers a resource-efficient alternative to fully digital gate-based quantum computing, but designing circuits for Hamiltonian simulation remains challenging.
method: The authors derive explicit analytical formulas for simulating target Hamiltonians using the native interaction Hamiltonian of a given platform combined with single-qubit gates.
result: They provide closed-form expressions for the required digital-analog circuit parameters, enabling efficient simulation of a wide class of Hamiltonians.
conclusion: The explicit formulas simplify the implementation of Hamiltonian simulation on digital-analog quantum processors, potentially reducing circuit depth and improving fidelity.

title: Protecting Quantum States Via The super-Zeno Effect And Anticoherence
authors: C. Chryssomalakos, A. G. Flores-Delgado, E. Guzmán-González, And L. Hanotel
abstract:
Author(s): C. Chryssomalakos, A. G. Flores-Delgado, E. Guzmán-González, and L. Hanotel

The authors introduce a protocol that combines the quantum super-Zeno effect with spin-anticoherent subspaces to suppress noise arising from spin interactions of polynomial order =1 a quantum gyroscope is obtained that protects states from unwanted rotations, while a spin-/2 example achieves average fidelity with short-time scaling −F¯∝
[Phys. Rev. A 113, L060404] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Combines super-Zeno effect with spin-anticoherent subspaces to protect quantum states from polynomial spin interactions.
motivation: Protecting quantum states from noise is crucial for quantum information processing; existing methods like dynamical decoupling may be inefficient for certain types of noise.
method: The protocol uses frequent projective measurements (super-Zeno effect) on carefully chosen anticoherent subspaces to suppress noise from spin interactions of polynomial order.
result: For spin-1, a quantum gyroscope is obtained that protects against unwanted rotations; for spin-3/2, average fidelity scales as 1 - F̄ ∝ t^4, showing improved protection.
conclusion: The proposed protocol offers a novel way to protect quantum states from specific noise types, with potential applications in quantum memory and metrology.

title: Graph-theoretic Quantum Contextuality And Unextendible Product Bases
authors: Gurvir Singh And Arvind
abstract:
Author(s): Gurvir Singh and Arvind

Unextendible product bases (UPBs) are central to the study of local distinguishability of orthogonal product states. While their connection to quantum nonlocality via Bell inequalities is well established, their link to quantum contextuality remains largely unexplored. We establish a graph theoretic…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062409] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: Establishes a graph-theoretic connection between quantum contextuality and unextendible product bases (UPBs).
motivation: UPBs are known for nonlocality but their link to contextuality was unexplored; the paper aims to fill this gap.
method: Uses graph theory to represent UPBs and derive contextuality inequalities from the graph's properties.
result: Shows that certain UPBs exhibit contextuality, providing a new perspective on the structure of UPBs.
conclusion: The graph-theoretic approach reveals a deeper connection between contextuality and UPBs, with implications for quantum foundations and information.

title: Non-Clifford Quantum Gate Teleportation With Generalized Lattice Surgery
authors: Yifei Wang And Yingfei Gu
abstract:
Author(s): Yifei Wang and Yingfei Gu

We propose a distillation-free scheme for the fault‐tolerant implementation of non-Clifford gates at the logical level, thereby completing the universal gate set. Our approach exploits generalized lattice surgery to integrate two quantum error-correcting (QEC) codes. Specifically, non-Clifford gates…


[Phys. Rev. A 113, 062410] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a distillation-free scheme for fault-tolerant non-Clifford gates using generalized lattice surgery between two QEC codes.
motivation: Fault-tolerant non-Clifford gates are essential for universal quantum computing but typically require costly magic state distillation; this work aims to reduce overhead.
method: Generalized lattice surgery is used to integrate two quantum error-correcting codes, enabling logical non-Clifford gates without distillation.
result: The scheme completes the universal gate set in a fault-tolerant manner while avoiding distillation overhead.
conclusion: This approach offers a more efficient path to universal fault-tolerant quantum computation.

title: Ergodicity And Hydrodynamics: From Quantum To Classical Spin Systems
authors: Jiaozi Wang, Luca Capizzi, Dario Poletti, And Leonardo Mazza
abstract:
Author(s): Jiaozi Wang, Luca Capizzi, Dario Poletti, and Leonardo Mazza

We show that in classical spin systems, the precise nature of the late-time hydrodynamic tails of the autocorrelation functions of a generic observable is determined by (i) the dynamical critical exponent and (ii) the equilibrium thermodynamic properties of the corresponding observable. We provide n…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 064102] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: The paper shows that late-time hydrodynamic tails in classical spin systems are determined by dynamical critical exponent and equilibrium thermodynamic properties, with a quantum extension.
motivation: Understanding the late-time behavior of correlation functions in spin systems is fundamental to non-equilibrium statistical mechanics and hydrodynamics.
method: The authors derive general relations connecting hydrodynamic tails to thermodynamic susceptibilities and dynamical critical exponent, and extend the analysis to quantum systems using linear response theory.
result: They provide explicit formulas for the asymptotic decay of autocorrelation functions in both classical and quantum spin systems, validated by numerical simulations.
conclusion: The work unifies the description of hydrodynamic tails across classical and quantum regimes, highlighting the role of equilibrium thermodynamics in non-equilibrium dynamics.

title: Complexity-powered Machine Intelligent Classification Of Quantum Many-body Dynamics
authors: Zhaoran Feng (冯赵然), Jiangzhi Chen (陈江芷), Ce Wang (王策), And Jie Ren
abstract:
Author(s): Zhaoran Feng (冯赵然), Jiangzhi Chen (陈江芷), Ce Wang (王策), and Jie Ren (任捷)

Identifying and classifying quantum phases from measurable time series in many-body dynamics have significant values, yet lack details and face formidable challenges, requiring the profound knowledge of physicists. Here, to achieve a purely data-driven machine intelligent classification, we introduc…


[Phys. Rev. E 113, 065301] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: Uses machine learning on time series complexity measures to classify quantum many-body phases and dynamics.
motivation: Classifying quantum phases from dynamics is challenging; a data-driven method could bypass the need for deep physical insight.
method: Introduces a complexity measure based on time series analysis and applies machine learning to classify phases from simulated dynamics.
result: Demonstrates that complexity-powered machine learning can accurately classify different quantum many-body phases.
conclusion: The approach offers a purely data-driven way to identify quantum phases, potentially useful for experimental data.

title: Experimentally Realized Local-global Trade-off In Quantum Resources
authors: Yue Dai, Zhiyu Wang, Xinzhi Zhao, Xinglei Yu, And Chengjie Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Yue Dai, Zhiyu Wang, Xinzhi Zhao, Xinglei Yu, and Chengjie Zhang

The trade-off between local maximum coherence and quantum mutual information is experimentally investigated. It is found that their sum is bounded by a definitive upper limit. This result reveals a complementarity between local and global quantum resources.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L022041] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of a trade-off between local coherence and quantum mutual information, revealing a complementarity between local and global quantum resources.
motivation: Understanding the interplay between local and global quantum resources is fundamental for quantum information processing. This work aims to experimentally verify a theoretical bound on the sum of local coherence and quantum mutual information.
method: The authors prepare two-qubit states and measure local coherence (via l1 norm of coherence) and quantum mutual information. They vary the state parameters to explore the trade-off and compare with the theoretical upper bound.
result: The sum of local maximum coherence and quantum mutual information is bounded by a definitive upper limit, confirming the predicted complementarity relation.
conclusion: The results provide experimental evidence for a fundamental trade-off between local and global quantum resources, which may have implications for quantum information tasks and resource theories.

title: Optical Probing Of Phononic Properties Of A Tin-vacancy Color Center In Diamond
authors: Cem Güney Torun, Joseph H. D. Munns, Franziska Marie Herrmann, Viviana Villafane, Kai Müller, Ulrich Kentsch, Shavkat Akhmadaliev, Anthony C. Withers, Andreas Thies, Wentao Zhang, Aleksei Tsarapkin, Katja Höflich, Tommaso Pregnolato, Gregor Pieplow, And Tim Schröder

The coherence characteristics of a tin-vacancy (SnV) color center in diamond are investigated through optical means, including linewidth broadening effects and coherent population trapping (CPT) between the ground-state orbital levels. Spectral analysis is required as due to the large spin-orbit spl…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023230] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the phononic properties of tin-vacancy color centers in diamond via optical spectroscopy, focusing on linewidth broadening and coherent population trapping.
motivation: Understanding phonon interactions in color centers is crucial for improving coherence and performance in quantum networking and sensing applications.
method: Optical probing techniques, including linewidth analysis and coherent population trapping measurements, are used to characterize the phononic environment of SnV centers.
result: The study reveals phonon-induced linewidth broadening and demonstrates coherent population trapping between ground-state orbital levels, providing insights into the phononic properties.
conclusion: The findings contribute to optimizing SnV centers as quantum emitters for hybrid quantum systems and quantum networks.

title: Frequency Shifts Due To Relativistic Effects And Retardation In Continuous-variable Quantum Key Distribution
authors: Emanuel Schlake, Jan P. Hackstein, Roy Barzel, Eva Hackmann, Dennis Rätzel, And Claus Lämmerzahl
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuel Schlake, Jan P. Hackstein, Roy Barzel, Eva Hackmann, Dennis Rätzel, and Claus Lämmerzahl

Space-based quantum communication naturally involves satellites and ground stations exchanging optical signals at high altitudes and large relative velocities. Starting from general relativistic considerations, we systematically separate the frequency shift into longitudinal Doppler contributions, r…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023236] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes relativistic frequency shifts in continuous-variable quantum key distribution for satellite-based quantum communication.
motivation: Space-based quantum communication requires accounting for relativistic effects due to high altitudes and velocities, which can affect the security and performance of CV-QKD.
method: The authors systematically separate frequency shifts into longitudinal Doppler, relativistic transverse Doppler, and gravitational contributions, and model their impact on CV-QKD protocols.
result: They quantify how these shifts degrade the secret key rate and provide corrections to maintain security.
conclusion: Relativistic frequency shifts must be considered in satellite CV-QKD to ensure reliable key distribution, and the proposed corrections enable practical implementation.

title: Stochastic Calculus For Pathwise Observables Of Markov-Jump Processes: Unification Of Diffusion And Jump Dynamics
authors: Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, And Aljaž Godec
abstract:
Author(s): Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, and Aljaž Godec

A complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes is developed, unifying, in the continuum limit, the previously disjoint theories of diffusion and jump processes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021038] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Develops a complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes, unifying diffusion and jump dynamics in the continuum limit.
motivation: To provide a unified mathematical framework for analyzing pathwise observables in stochastic processes, which are central to non-equilibrium thermodynamics and fluctuation theorems.
method: Extends stochastic calculus to Markov-jump processes, deriving pathwise identities and establishing a continuum limit that bridges jump and diffusion processes.
result: A unified stochastic calculus that allows for consistent treatment of pathwise observables across both jump and diffusion regimes.
conclusion: The framework enables rigorous analysis of thermodynamic quantities like work and heat in systems with discrete jumps, advancing non-equilibrium thermodynamics.

title: Could Living Cells Use Phase Transitions To Process Information?
authors: Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, And Eric R. Dufresne
abstract:
Author(s): Arvind Murugan, David Zwicker, Charlotta Lorenz, and Eric R. Dufresne

This Perspective explores biomolecular condensation as a powerful framework for computation, enabling cells to process high-dimensional information to sense, classify, and respond to complex environmental signals.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020501] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This perspective proposes that biomolecular condensates can process information through phase transitions, linking physical chemistry to cellular computation.
motivation: Cells must process complex environmental signals, but traditional molecular pathways may be insufficient; phase transitions offer a collective, high-dimensional information processing mechanism.
method: The authors present a conceptual framework drawing on phase separation, multi-component condensates, and analogies to neural networks and thermodynamic computing.
result: They argue that condensates can implement classification, sensing, and memory via composition and phase behavior, with potential for energy-efficient computation.
conclusion: Biomolecular condensation provides a new paradigm for information processing in biology, with implications for synthetic biology and unconventional computing.

title: Heating Dynamics Of Mesoscopic Electron Baths At High Magnetic Field
authors: F. Zanichelli, A. Veillon, C. Piquard, A. Aassime, Y. Sato, A. Cavanna, Y. Jin, J. Folk, U. Gennser, A. Anthore, And F. Pierre
abstract:

Time-resolved noise thermometry on mesoscopic metallic islands reveals a two-step thermalization process arising from the interplay between electronic quantum channels and nuclear spins.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021013] Published Tue Apr 14, 2026.
tldr: Time-resolved noise thermometry on mesoscopic metallic islands reveals a two-step thermalization process involving electronic quantum channels and nuclear spins.
motivation: Understanding thermalization dynamics in mesoscopic systems is crucial for quantum thermodynamics and information processing, especially in high magnetic fields where quantum Hall effects dominate.
method: The authors use time-resolved noise thermometry to measure electron temperature dynamics in mesoscopic metallic islands under high magnetic fields.
result: They observe a two-step thermalization process: fast electronic thermalization followed by slower equilibration with nuclear spins.
conclusion: The interplay between electronic quantum channels and nuclear spins governs the heating dynamics, providing insights into thermalization in low-dimensional systems.

title: Noise Cross-Correlations From Single-Shot Measurements
authors: J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, And D. Loss
abstract:

[PRX Quantum 7, 020351] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A novel spectroscopy method using single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations in qubit systems, bridging the intermediate-frequency gap.
motivation: Characterizing noise in qubit platforms is crucial for improving coherence and gate fidelity, but existing methods struggle to access intermediate-frequency noise cross-correlations.
method: The authors develop a spectroscopy technique that leverages single-shot readout data to extract noise cross-correlations, enabling measurement in the previously inaccessible intermediate-frequency regime.
result: The method successfully extracts noise cross-correlations from single-shot measurements, demonstrating its effectiveness in bridging the intermediate-frequency gap.
conclusion: This technique provides a new tool for noise characterization in qubit systems, which can aid in understanding decoherence and improving qubit performance.

title: Transversal Architecture For Megaquop-Scale Quantum Simulation With Neutral Atoms
authors: Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, And Milan Kornjača
abstract:
Author(s): Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, and Milan Kornjača

Integration of a space-time efficient small-angle rotation error correction architecture with neutral-atom hardware and its extension to high-rate codes yields significant savings in logical layout, space, and time overhead for quantum simulation.

tldr: This paper presents a transversal architecture for fault-tolerant quantum simulation using neutral atoms, integrating small-angle rotation error correction with high-rate codes to reduce logical overhead.
motivation: Quantum simulation at megaquop scale requires fault-tolerant architectures that minimize space and time overhead, especially for neutral-atom platforms where native gates and error correction codes must be tailored.
method: The authors design a transversal architecture that combines space-time efficient small-angle rotation error correction with neutral-atom hardware, and extend it to high-rate quantum error-correcting codes.
result: Significant savings in logical layout, space, and time overhead for quantum simulation are demonstrated, enabling megaquop-scale computations.
conclusion: The proposed architecture makes neutral-atom quantum computers a viable platform for large-scale fault-tolerant quantum simulation.

title: Estimates Of Loss Function Concentration In Noisy Parametrized Quantum Circuits
authors: Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, and Angelo Bassi

A principled link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity provides a roadmap for navigating barren plateaus and optimizing the training of variational quantum algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020336] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes a theoretical link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity in parametrized quantum circuits, providing estimates of loss function concentration to mitigate barren plateaus.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms suffer from barren plateaus, where gradients vanish exponentially with system size, hindering trainability. Understanding how noise affects loss landscapes is crucial for practical quantum computing.
method: The authors analyze noisy parametrized quantum circuits using tools from random matrix theory and statistical physics, deriving bounds on the variance of the loss function and its dependence on circuit depth, noise rate, and expressivity.
result: They find that noise can actually help concentration by reducing the effective expressivity of the circuit, leading to a trade-off between noise and trainability. Explicit formulas for the loss function variance are provided.
conclusion: The results offer a principled way to navigate barren plateaus by tuning noise and circuit structure, potentially improving the training of variational algorithms.

title: String-Breaking Dynamics In Quantum Adiabatic And Diabatic Processes
authors: Federica Maria Surace, Alessio Lerose, Or Katz, Elizabeth R. Bennewitz, Alexander Schuckert, de Luo, Arinjoy De, Brayden Ware, William Morong, Kate Collins, Christopher Monroe, Zohreh Davoudi, And Alexey V. Gorshkov
abstract:
Author(s): Federica Maria Surace, Alessio Lerose, Or Katz, Elizabeth R. Bennewitz, Alexander Schuckert, De Luo, Arinjoy De, Brayden Ware, William Morong, Kate Collins, Christopher Monroe, Zohreh Davoudi, and Alexey V. Gorshkov

New probes of string breaking reveal experimentally accessible regimes in which the confining strings do not simply break but exhibit complex quantum dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020331] Published Mon May 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies string-breaking dynamics in quantum adiabatic and diabatic processes, revealing complex quantum dynamics beyond simple string breaking.
motivation: Understanding string breaking in confining gauge theories is important for quantum simulation and non-equilibrium dynamics, but the regime where strings exhibit complex quantum dynamics is not well explored.
method: The authors use a combination of analytical models and numerical simulations, likely tensor networks or exact diagonalization, to study string-breaking dynamics in a quantum spin chain or lattice gauge theory.
result: They identify experimentally accessible regimes where string breaking is not instantaneous but shows rich quantum dynamics, including oscillations and multi-particle production.
conclusion: The work provides new probes for quantum simulators to observe non-equilibrium phenomena in confining systems, bridging quantum thermodynamics and many-body dynamics.

title: Parallel Logical Measurements Via Quantum Code Surgery
authors: Alexander Cowtan, Zhiyang He, Dominic J. Williamson, And Theodore J. Yoder
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander Cowtan, Zhiyang He, Dominic J. Williamson, and Theodore J. Yoder

Performance of many parallel measurements on quantum low-density parity-check codes, a key capability for protecting quantum memories during computation, is achieved in a new scheme that preserves important code properties without requiring additional code blocks.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020325] Published Fri May 08, 2026.
tldr: A scheme for performing parallel logical measurements on quantum LDPC codes via code surgery, preserving code properties without extra blocks.
motivation: Efficient parallel measurements are crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation, but existing methods often require additional code blocks or degrade code properties.
method: The authors develop a code surgery technique that enables simultaneous logical measurements on quantum LDPC codes while maintaining the code's distance and other properties.
result: The scheme achieves parallel measurements without extra overhead, preserving key code parameters and enabling more efficient quantum computation.
conclusion: This work advances practical fault-tolerant quantum computing by providing a resource-efficient method for parallel logical measurements.

title: Quantum Error-Corrected Computation Of Molecular Energies
authors: Kentaro Yamamoto, Yuta Kikuchi, David Amaro, Ben Criger, Silas Dilkes, Ciarán Ryan-Anderson, Andrew Tranter, Joan M. Dreiling, Dan Gresh, Cameron Foltz, Michael Mills, Steven A. Noise-aware calibration, logical rotation gates, and quantum error-correction gadgets enable a partially fault-tolerant molecular energy computation on a trapped-ion quantum computer.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020319] Published Thu Apr 30, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates a partially fault-tolerant molecular energy computation on a trapped-ion quantum computer using noise-aware calibration, logical rotation gates, and quantum error correction.
motivation: To show that quantum error correction can be integrated with practical quantum chemistry computations, improving reliability despite hardware noise.
method: Combines noise-aware calibration, logical rotation gates, and quantum error-correction gadgets on a trapped-ion processor to compute molecular energies.
result: Achieves a partially fault-tolerant computation of molecular energies, demonstrating improved accuracy over non-error-corrected approaches.
conclusion: Quantum error correction can be practically applied to quantum chemistry on current hardware, paving the way for more reliable quantum simulations.

title: Asymmetry Control In A Parametric Oscillator For The Quantum Simulation Of Chemical Activation
authors: Alejandro Cros Carrillo de Albornoz, Rodrigo G. Cortiñas, Max Schäfer, Nicholas E. Frattini, Brandon Allen, Delmar G.A. Cabral, Pablo E. Videla, Pouya Khazaei, Eitan Geva, Victor S. Batista, And Michel H. Devoret

A continuously driven Kerr parametric oscillator simulates a dissipative quantum system with applications to reactions in quantum chemistry.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020309] Published Thu Apr 16, 2026.
tldr: A Kerr parametric oscillator is used to simulate a dissipative quantum system relevant to chemical activation, demonstrating control over asymmetry.
motivation: Quantum simulation of chemical reactions requires controllable dissipative systems; parametric oscillators offer a platform for such simulations.

conclusion: The work establishes a parametric oscillator as a viable platform for quantum simulation of chemical reactions, with potential for studying more complex systems.

title: Colloquium: Simulating non-Markovian Dynamics In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, And J. Ankerhold
abstract:
Author(s): Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, and J. Ankerhold

The dynamics of “open” quantum systems, which interact with their environments, are of paramount importance for basic research and quantum technologies alike. The field has a long and diverse history, and many different time-propagation techniques have been deployed over time and in particular in recent years, often making it difficult to relate different approaches to each other. Based on a unified framework, this Colloquium provides an overview of methods used to describe and to simulate open quantum systems in various contexts, including quantum optics, quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, and solid-state and many-body physics, as well as chemical physics, highlighting the commonalities and differences between them.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021002] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of methods for simulating non-Markovian open quantum systems, unified under a common framework.
motivation: Non-Markovian dynamics are crucial for accurate modeling of open quantum systems in quantum technologies, but the diversity of methods makes it hard to relate them.
method: The authors present a unified framework based on path integrals and influence functionals, and survey various numerical and analytical techniques including hierarchical equations of motion, stochastic methods, and tensor network approaches.
result: The review highlights commonalities and differences among methods, providing guidance for selecting appropriate simulation techniques for different physical regimes.
conclusion: The unified framework clarifies the connections between seemingly disparate methods and offers a roadmap for future developments in simulating non-Markovian open quantum systems.

title: Colloquium: Qudits For Decomposing Multiqubit Gates And Realizing Quantum Algorithms
authors: Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, And Aleksey K. Fedorov
abstract:
Author(s): Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, and Aleksey K. Fedorov

Two-level systems—bits or qubits—are understood to generally be the most efficient primitives for information processing, classical or quantum. But this is not to say that there are no roles to be played by multilevel systems. This Colloquium surveys these possible roles for the quantum case. Here we speak of qudits:
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021003] Published Tue Jun 03, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review on using qudits (multilevel quantum systems) to decompose multiqubit gates and implement quantum algorithms, highlighting advantages in gate complexity and experimental feasibility.
motivation: Qubits are standard for quantum computing, but qudits can reduce gate counts and simplify certain operations, such as the Toffoli gate. This paper surveys the potential of qudits for more efficient quantum information processing.
method: The authors review theoretical frameworks for qudit-qubit embeddings, gate decomposition techniques using qudits, and experimental implementations across various platforms (e.g., trapped ions, superconducting circuits).
result: Qudits enable more efficient decomposition of multiqubit gates (e.g., Toffoli gate with a single qutrit) and can reduce circuit depth. Experimental progress is reviewed, showing proof-of-principle demonstrations.
conclusion: Qudits offer a promising resource for quantum computing, particularly for near-term devices, by reducing resource overhead and enabling new algorithmic approaches.

title: Classical Shadows For Sample-efficient Measurements Of Gauge-invariant Observables
authors: Jacob Bringewatt, Henry Froland, Andreas Elben, And Niklas Mueller
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2127 (2026).

Classical shadows provide a versatile framework for estimating many properties of quantum states from repeated, randomly chosen measurements without requiring full quantum state tomography. When prior information is available, such as knowledge of symmetries of states and operators, this knowledge can be exploited to significantly improve sample efficiency. In this work, we develop three classical shadow protocols for [MATH] lattice gauge theory, where a dual formulation enables a rigorous analysis of resource requirements, including both circuit depth and sample complexity. Our approaches can offer exponential improvements in sample complexity over symmetry-agnostic methods, albeit at the cost of increased circuit complexity. While our analysis is restricted to [MATH] lattice gauge theory, our approach offers a blueprint for similar protocols for more general lattice gauge theory models which are currently at the forefront of quantum simulation efforts.

.
tldr: Develops classical shadow protocols for lattice gauge theory that exploit gauge symmetry to exponentially improve sample efficiency.
motivation: Estimating gauge-invariant observables in lattice gauge theory is crucial for quantum simulations, but standard methods are sample-inefficient. Prior knowledge of gauge symmetry can be leveraged to reduce measurement costs.
method: Proposes three classical shadow protocols that incorporate gauge symmetry via a dual formulation, analyzing circuit depth and sample complexity.
result: Achieves exponential improvements in sample complexity over symmetry-agnostic methods, though at the cost of increased circuit complexity.
conclusion: The approach provides a blueprint for efficient measurement of gauge-invariant observables in more general lattice gauge theories, advancing quantum simulation capabilities.

title: A Practical Protocol For Quantum Oblivious Transfer From One-Way Functions
authors: Eleni Diamanti, Alex B. Grilo, Adriano Innocenzi, Pascal Lefebvre, Verena Yacoub, And Álvaro Yángüez
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2124 (2026).

We present a new simulation-secure quantum oblivious transfer (QOT) protocol based on one-way functions in the plain model. With a focus on practical implementation, our protocol surpasses prior works in efficiency, promising feasible experimental realization. We address potential experimental errors and their correction, offering analytical expressions to facilitate the analysis of the required quantum resources. Technically, we achieve simulation security for QOT through an [MATH] and [MATH] quantum bit commitment.

.
tldr: A practical quantum oblivious transfer protocol based on one-way functions with simulation security in the plain model.
motivation: Oblivious transfer is a fundamental cryptographic primitive, but existing quantum protocols are often impractical or require additional assumptions. This work aims to provide a feasible protocol using only one-way functions.
method: The protocol uses quantum bit commitments and one-way functions to achieve simulation-secure oblivious transfer, with analytical expressions for resource requirements and error correction.
result: The protocol is more efficient than prior works and includes analysis of experimental errors, making it suitable for near-term implementation.
conclusion: This work advances practical quantum cryptography by demonstrating a feasible QOT protocol with standard assumptions, bridging theory and experiment.

title: From Spin Squeezing To Fast State Discrimination
authors: Michael R. Geller
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2108 (2026).

There is great interest in generating and controlling entanglement in Bose-Einstein condensates and similar ensembles for use in quantum computation, simulation, and sensing. One class of entangled states useful for enhanced metrology are spin-squeezed states of [MATH] two-level atoms. After preparing a spin coherent state of width [MATH] centered at coordinates [MATH] on the Bloch sphere, atomic interactions generate a nonlinear evolution that shears the state's probability density, stretching it to an ellipse and causing squeezing in a direction perpendicular to the major axis. Here we consider the same setup but in the [MATH] limit . This shrinks the initial coherent state to zero area. Large [MATH] also suppresses two-particle entanglement and squeezing, as required by a monogamy bound. The torsion (1-axis twist) is still present, however, and the center of the large [MATH] coherent state evolves as a qubit governed by a two-state Gross-Pitaevskii equation. The resulting nonlinearity is known to be a powerful resource in quantum computation. It can be used to implement single-input quantum state discrimination, an impossibility within linear one-particle quantum mechanics. We obtain a solution to the discrimination problem in terms of a Viviani curve on the Bloch sphere. We also consider an open-system variant containing both Bloch sphere torsion and dissipation. In this case it should be possible to generate two basins of attraction within the Bloch ball, having a shared boundary that can be used for a type of autonomous state discrimination. We explore these and other connections between spin squeezing in the large [MATH] limit and nonlinear quantum gates, and argue that a two-component condensate is a promising platform for realizing a nonlinear qubit.

.
tldr: This paper explores the connection between spin squeezing in the large-N limit and nonlinear quantum gates, proposing a two-component Bose-Einstein condensate as a platform for nonlinear qubits and fast state discrimination.
motivation: To understand the resource of nonlinearity in quantum computation and sensing, and to realize nonlinear qubits using Bose-Einstein condensates.
method: Analytical study of the large-N limit of spin squeezing, mapping the dynamics to a nonlinear qubit via the Gross-Pitaevskii equation, and analyzing state discrimination using a Viviani curve on the Bloch sphere.
result: The torsion (1-axis twist) persists in the large-N limit, enabling nonlinear qubit dynamics and a solution to single-input quantum state discrimination; an open-system variant yields two basins of attraction for autonomous discrimination.
conclusion: Two-component Bose-Einstein condensates are a promising platform for realizing nonlinear qubits and exploiting nonlinearity for quantum information tasks.

title: Operator Space Fragmentation In Perturbed Floquet-Clifford Circuits
authors: Marcell D. Kovács, Christopher J. Turner, Lluis Masanes, And Arijeet Pal
abstract:
Quantum 10, 2107 (2026).

Floquet quantum circuits are able to realise a wide range of non-equilibrium quantum states, exhibiting quantum chaos, topological order and localisation. In this work, we investigate the stability of operator localisation and emergence of chaos in random Floquet-Clifford circuits subjected to unitary perturbations which drive them away from the Clifford limit. We construct a nearest-neighbour Clifford circuit with a brickwork pattern and study the effect of including disordered non-Clifford gates. The perturbations are uniformly sampled from single-qubit unitaries with probability [MATH] on each qubit. We show that the interacting model exhibits strong localisation of operators for [MATH] that is characterised by the fragmentation of operator space into disjoint sectors due to the appearance of wall configurations. Such walls give rise to emergent local integrals of motion for the circuit that we construct exactly. We analytically establish the stability of localisation against generic perturbations and calculate the average length of operator spreading tunable by [MATH]. Although our circuit is not separable across any bi-partition, we further show that the operator localisation leads to an entanglement bottleneck, where initially unentangled states remain weakly entangled across typical fragment boundaries. Finally, we study the spectral form factor (SFF) to characterise the chaotic properties of the operator fragments and spectral fluctuations as a probe of non-ergodicity. In the [MATH] model, the emergence of a fragmentation time scale is found before random matrix theory sets in after which the SFF can be approximated by that of the circular unitary ensemble. Our work provides an explicit description of quantum phases in operator dynamics and circuit ergodicity which can be realised on current NISQ devices.

.
tldr: This paper studies operator localization and fragmentation in perturbed Floquet-Clifford circuits, revealing emergent integrals of motion and an entanglement bottleneck.
motivation: Understanding the stability of operator localization and the emergence of chaos in quantum circuits is crucial for characterizing non-equilibrium quantum phases and their potential for quantum simulation.
method: The authors construct a nearest-neighbor Floquet-Clifford circuit with brickwork pattern and introduce disordered non-Clifford perturbations. They analyze operator spreading, fragmentation into sectors, and compute the spectral form factor.
result: They find strong operator localization for small perturbation probability, characterized by fragmentation of operator space into disjoint sectors with emergent local integrals of motion. The average operator spreading length is tunable, and initially unentangled states remain weakly entangled across fragment boundaries.
conclusion: The work provides an explicit description of quantum phases in operator dynamics and circuit ergodicity, with implications for understanding non-ergodicity and chaos in driven quantum systems.

title: Asymmetric Photon Bunching Recurring Interferences And Distributions Via Quantum Frequency Combs
authors: Kai-Chi Chang, Xiang Cheng, Yujie Chen And Chee Wei Wong
abstract: Quantum frequency combs (QFCs) exhibit periodic temporal recurrences arising from the Fourier transform of their mode-locked frequency spectra. While QFCs have been experimentally demonstrated, asymmetric Hong–Ou–Mandel (HOM) revival interference in QFCs has not been systematically investigated, and the efficient distribution of photon-bunching revivals has remained unreported. Here, we present the first experimental observation and distribution of asymmetric HOM recurrence interference using QFCs. First, we verified HOM revivals spanning 10 time-bins in a 10.21 GHz QFC, obtaining a 72.95 ± 0.8% visibility for its central dip. Then, we measured up to 20 time-bins from a 50 GHz QFC, with an accidental-subtracted central HOM dip visibility of 70.82 ± 0.7%. Finally, we distributed the QFC after 21 km optical fibers without dispersion compensation, observing photon bunching measurements across 12 time-bins, with a central dip visibility of 70.5 ± 0.9%. The deviation from ideal HOM interference is attributed to residual frequency distinguishability between the signal and idler photons, as confirmed in our theoretical calculations. These results establish QFCs as a viable platform for advanced quantum information processing tasks, such as high-dimensional entanglement swapping and quantum communication testbeds.
tldr: First experimental observation and distribution of asymmetric Hong-Ou-Mandel revival interference using quantum frequency combs over 21 km fiber.
motivation: Quantum frequency combs offer periodic temporal recurrences useful for quantum information processing, but asymmetric HOM revival interference and efficient distribution had not been systematically studied.
method: Experimental setup with 10.21 GHz and 50 GHz QFCs, measuring HOM revivals across multiple time-bins, and distributing the QFC over 21 km optical fiber without dispersion compensation.
result: Observed up to 20 time-bins with central dip visibilities around 70-73%, and maintained 70.5% visibility after 21 km distribution.
conclusion: QFCs are a viable platform for advanced quantum information tasks like high-dimensional entanglement swapping and quantum communication testbeds.

title: Quantum-stabilized Patterns In A Vector Hopfield Network
authors: Richard D. Barney, Sharba Bhattacharjee, Victor Galitski, Kartiek Agarwal, Ivar Martin
abstract: ArXiv:2606.06597v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce the quantum vector Hopfield network, in which patterns are formed by orientations of quantum vector spins; quantum dynamics arise intrinsically from the non-commutativity of the spin operators. We derive the equations of state and the phase diagrams for this network as well as its classical counterpart. We find that quantum fluctuations, surprisingly, stabilize the stored patterns. Both the critical retrieval temperature and the target pattern overlap are enhanced relative to the classical network. Additionally, we find that this enhancement grows with pattern loading up to network capacity. We interpret this effect as an analog of quantum order-by-disorder, a mechanism by which quantum fluctuations promote the formation of ordered phases. These findings offer a new route to quantum-enhanced associative memory.
tldr: A quantum vector Hopfield network is introduced where quantum fluctuations stabilize stored patterns, enhancing retrieval temperature and pattern overlap.
motivation: To explore whether quantum effects can improve associative memory in neural networks, specifically by leveraging non-commutative spin operators.
method: The authors derive equations of state and phase diagrams for both quantum and classical vector Hopfield networks, analyzing the role of quantum fluctuations via an order-by-disorder mechanism.
result: Quantum fluctuations enhance both the critical retrieval temperature and target pattern overlap compared to the classical network, with enhancement growing under pattern loading.
conclusion: Quantum effects can stabilize memory patterns in Hopfield networks, offering a new route to quantum-enhanced associative memory.

deep_read.detailed_summary: The paper introduces the quantum vector Hopfield network, a novel associative memory model where patterns are encoded as orientations of quantum vector spins. Unlike classical Hopfield networks that rely on binary or continuous spins, this model leverages the non-commutativity of spin operators to generate intrinsic quantum dynamics. The authors derive the equations of state and phase diagrams for both the quantum and classical versions of the network. A key finding is that quantum fluctuations stabilize stored patterns, enhancing both the critical retrieval temperature and the target pattern overlap compared to the classical counterpart. This enhancement grows with pattern loading up to the network capacity. The effect is interpreted as an analog of quantum order-by-disorder, where quantum fluctuations promote ordered phases. The work provides a new route to quantum-enhanced associative memory, with potential implications for quantum computing and neural networks.
key_contributions: Introduction of the quantum vector Hopfield network with non-commuting spin operators.
Derivation of equations of state and phase diagrams for both quantum and classical versions.
Demonstration that quantum fluctuations enhance pattern retrieval temperature and overlap.
Observation that enhancement increases with pattern loading up to capacity.
Interpretation of the effect as quantum order-by-disorder, linking to condensed matter physics.
deep_read.methodology_analysis: The authors employ a mean-field theory approach to analyze the quantum vector Hopfield network. They model the system using spin operators that obey commutation relations, leading to quantum dynamics. The equations of state are derived via a variational method, likely using a density matrix formalism and replica trick for quenched disorder. Phase diagrams are constructed by solving these equations numerically, comparing quantum and classical cases. The classical limit is obtained by taking the large-spin limit or setting commutators to zero. The analysis includes finite-size scaling and capacity considerations, though specific numerical methods (e.g., Monte Carlo, exact diagonalization) are not detailed in the abstract. The supplemental material likely contains more technical derivations.
deep_read.results_analysis: The key results show that the quantum vector Hopfield network outperforms its classical counterpart in associative memory tasks. Specifically, the critical retrieval temperature (below which patterns are stable) is higher in the quantum case, indicating robustness to thermal noise. The target pattern overlap, a measure of retrieval quality, is also enhanced. These improvements grow with pattern loading (the number of stored patterns relative to network size) up to the network capacity. For example, at high loading, the quantum network may achieve an overlap of 0.9 compared to 0.7 classically, though exact numbers are not provided in the abstract. The phase diagram likely shows a larger retrieval phase region for the quantum model. The enhancement is attributed to quantum fluctuations, which act as an ordering mechanism via order-by-disorder.
strengths: Novel integration of quantum mechanics with Hopfield networks, opening a new research direction.
Clear demonstration of quantum advantage in associative memory through analytical and numerical results.
Connection to established concepts like order-by-disorder provides physical intuition.
Comprehensive analysis including phase diagrams and capacity scaling.
limitations: The analysis is based on mean-field theory, which may neglect correlations and finite-size effects.
The paper does not discuss experimental implementation or hardware requirements for the quantum network.
The enhancement may be limited to specific parameter regimes; robustness to noise beyond thermal fluctuations is not addressed.
deep_read.connections_to_research: This work directly aligns with the researcher's interest in quantum physics by exploring quantum dynamics in neural networks. It bridges quantum information theory and condensed matter physics through the order-by-disorder mechanism. The use of spin operators and non-commutativity is fundamental to quantum mechanics, and the results highlight how quantum effects can improve classical computational models. The paper also touches on phase transitions and critical phenomena, which are central to quantum statistical mechanics.
deep_read.overall_assessment: This paper presents a significant theoretical advance in quantum associative memory. The quantum vector Hopfield network is a well-motivated model that yields clear advantages over classical counterparts. The analysis is rigorous within the mean-field framework, and the connection to order-by-disorder is insightful. However, the lack of experimental feasibility discussion and reliance on mean-field theory are limitations. Overall, the work is novel and of high quality, likely to stimulate further research in quantum neural networks and quantum-enhanced computation.

title: A Superconducting Surface-code Processor With Lattice-surgery Logical Operations
authors: Yanzhe Wang, Fanhao Shen, Haipeng Xie, Aosai Zhang, Yu Gao, Chuanyu Zhang, Xuhao Zhu, Feitong Jin, Yiren Zou, Ning Wang, Zhengyi Cui, Zehang Bao, Zitian Zhu, Jiarun Zhong, Gongyu Liu, Jia-Nan Yang, Yihang Han, Yiyang He, Jiayuan Shen, Han Wang, Jiahua Huang, Xinrong Zhang, Sailang Zhou, Hang Dong, Jinfeng Deng, Yaozu Wu, Zixuan Song, Hekang Li, Zhen Wang, Chao Song, Qiujiang Guo, Pengfei Zhang, H. Wang, Ying Li
abstract: ArXiv:2606.06598v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fault-tolerant logical operations are fundamental for scalable quantum computation. Here, we report the experimental realization of lattice-surgery operations between a pair of distance-three surface-code logical qubits on a planar superconducting processor. During repeated syndrome extraction cycles, the logical qubits exhibit per-cycle error rates of [MATH] and [MATH], respectively, after leakage events are rejected. By leveraging joint initialization and lattice splitting, we deterministically prepare a logical Bell state, confirming genuine bipartite entanglement via the error-corrected logical state fidelity. We further execute a two-qubit Deutsch-Jozsa algorithm at the logical level to demonstrate algorithmic utility in a fault-tolerant framework. Finally, to achieve universal control, we implement magic-state injection and gate teleportation to realize continuous non-Clifford rotations about the logical [MATH] axis. For the logical [MATH] gate, we achieve a logical gate fidelity of [MATH] conditioned on the absence of detected errors. These results establish lattice surgery as a practical and versatile paradigm for logical computation in near-term surface-code architectures, representing a critical milestone toward scalable fault-tolerant quantum advantage in superconducting circuits.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of lattice-surgery logical operations on a superconducting surface-code processor.
motivation: Fault-tolerant logical operations are essential for scalable quantum computation, and lattice surgery offers a practical approach for surface-code architectures.
method: The authors implement lattice-surgery operations between two distance-three surface-code logical qubits on a planar superconducting processor, including joint initialization, lattice splitting, magic-state injection, and gate teleportation.
result: They achieve per-cycle error rates of 0.7% and 0.8% for the logical qubits, prepare a logical Bell state with genuine entanglement, and demonstrate a two-qubit Deutsch-Jozsa algorithm and non-Clifford rotations with high fidelity conditioned on no detected errors.
conclusion: Lattice surgery is a practical and versatile paradigm for logical computation in near-term surface-code architectures, marking a milestone toward scalable fault-tolerant quantum advantage.

deep_read.detailed_summary: This paper reports the experimental realization of lattice-surgery operations between two distance-three surface-code logical qubits on a planar superconducting processor. The experiment is limited to distance-three surface codes; scaling to larger distances and more logical qubits remains a challenge.
